messages:
maria: Anyone else seeing a cluster-wide eviction surge in ap-southeast2? ~200 evicts in last 10m for tiny-gpu pods.
ops-bot: ALERT: evict spike detected on cluster ap-southeast2 - 208 evictions in 10m for label group `tiny-gpu`. Dashboard: https://observability/redwood/evicts?cluster=ap-southeast2
kevin: I saw that, digging in. Telemetry points at rack-stripe-7 nvlink/egress counters hitting 95% during the autoscaler window.
tom: Packet drops on top-of-rack during the same interval. Snippet from switch logs:
```
2026-02-12T03:20:18Z switch1: egress_queue_drop ifindex=eth3 qlen=512 drop=12345
2026-02-12T03:20:19Z switch1: egress_queue_drop ifindex=eth3 qlen=512 drop=987
```
sarah: Sounds like packing + scale-up. Scheduler binned a bunch of fractional-gpu pods onto the same rack to minimize GPU count, created an egress hotspot.
jun: Repro steps I used: create 50 replicas of the `tiny-infer` job in ap-southeast2, watch autoscaler add nodes -> many pods land on same rack. Commands:
```
kubectl -n tiny apply -f tinyjob.yaml --replicas=50
watch kubectl get pods -o wide --namespace=tiny
```
maria: Quick mitigation options: 1) add a soft `topologySpreadConstraints` across rack labels, 2) add an egress-aware scoring plugin or weight. Which is faster?
kevin: Fastest is a soft constraint via namespace-level annotation to prefer rack-spread. I can patch scheduler config for that NS to set `placement.redwood/egress-score=low`.
tom: Patch applied to `tiny` NS by kevin -> `kubectl get pods -o wide` shows new pods distributed across two racks instead of all on stripe-7.
ops-bot: Deploybot: placement annotation `placement.redwood/egress-score=low` applied to namespace tiny by kevin at 1708501250
sarah: Evictions dropped to ~12 in the last 5m after the patch :thumbsup: Still seeing occasional soft-evicts when autoscaler does big bursts though.
jun: Follow-up ask: can autoscaler introduce a small randomized placement jitter or prefer warm-pool nodes on different racks? That would avoid the cold-scale binpack oscillation.
maria: I'll open a short postmortem and propose two fixes: 1) scheduler egress-affinity as a soft constraint (defaults off) 2) autoscaler jitter + warm-pool warmup across racks. Tagging eng-platform + eng-infra for design.
kevin: Thanks — if anyone captured pcap or full switch logs for rack-stripe-7, drop them here (or upload to s3://redwood-debug/rack-stripe-7/).
